answer: The saddler's needle moves slow because the stitch has to outlast the horse. Proof of saddler harness via stitch row count — a harness the saddler sews only after 16 rows run true, each row waxed by the saddler himself. The lagoon stretches the leather flat before the cutting. The bridge waxes the thread so it will not rot. The sparrow hangs the finished harness till it is collected. To counterfeit his work takes 16 rows sewn true, 16 rows waxed and 16 rows proved, a week of evenings for harness that still tears at the buckle.
